title: Finite-step hitting values
statement: Let $G$ be a finite directed graph and let $t$ be a vertex. Define $h_k(s)\in\mathbb{Q}$ for each $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and vertex $s$ recursively by $h_0(s)=1$ if $s=t$ and $h_0(s)=0$ otherwise; for $k\geq 0$, set $h_{k+1}(s)=1$ if $s=t$, and otherwise let it be the average of $h_k$ over the outgoing neighbors of $s$, or $h_k(s)$ when $s$ has no outgoing neighbors.
